{{Short description|British mathematics education project}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2021}}

'''Count On''' is a major [[mathematics education]] project in the [[United Kingdom]] which was announced by [[Secretary of State for Education|education secretary]] [[David Blunkett]] at the end of 2000. It was the follow-on to [[Maths Year 2000]] which was the UK's contribution to [[UNICEF]]'s [[World Mathematical Year]].<ref>{{citation|title=English pupils lag behind in maths|publisher=[[BBC News]]|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/education/1055704.stm|date=5 December 2000}}.</ref>

Count On had two main strands:
* The website www.counton.org<ref>{{citation|title=My Media: Kate Scarborough|journal=[[The Guardian]]|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2006/jul/31/mondaymediasection4|date=31 July 2006}}.</ref> which won the 2002 [[BETT]] prize for best free online learning resource.<ref>{{citation|title=Deputy logs on to £100,000|journal=[[Times Educational Supplement]]|url=http://www.tes.co.uk/teaching-resource/Deputy-logs-on-to-pounds-100-000-358319/|date=18 January 2002|access-date=24 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121005094334/http://www.tes.co.uk/teaching-resource/Deputy-logs-on-to-pounds-100-000-358319/|archive-date=5 October 2012|url-status=dead}}.</ref>
* "MathFests", which were maths funfairs held around the country, aimed particularly at those who would not normally come into contact with mathematical ideas.<ref>{{citation|title=No doubt about it - we're addicted to maths|journal=[[Times Educational Supplement]]|url=http://www.tes.co.uk/article.aspx?storycode=342720|date=19 January 2001|access-date=24 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121005094344/http://www.tes.co.uk/article.aspx?storycode=342720|archive-date=5 October 2012|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

==Popularisation of Mathematics==
''Count On'' and ''Maths Year 2000'' were some of the first big Popularisation of Mathematics projects. Others are listed below.

===International===
* [[World Mathematical Year 2000]] [https://web.archive.org/web/20130113071154/http://wmy2000.math.jussieu.fr/]
* Statistics 2013 [http://statistics2013.org/]
* [[World Maths Day]] (orig. Australian) - next one is 6 March 2013 [https://web.archive.org/web/20110925091442/http://www.worldmathsday.com/]

===Australia===
* [[World Maths Day]][https://web.archive.org/web/20110925091442/http://www.worldmathsday.com/]

===Nigeria===
* [[National Mathematics Year]]

* Paul Boron [http://www.paulborons.com/]

===United Kingdom===
* Maths Year 2000 Scotland
* Maths Cymru (Wales)
